key_insight: This paper shows that neural operators can be constructed from standard numerical discretizations, suggesting they may learn the underlying finite-element/finite-difference scheme rather than only the continuous PDE operator.
engineering_relevance: It offers a more parameter-efficient and theoretically grounded path to surrogate models for PDE-based engineering simulations, especially when training data are generated numerically.
method: Approximate or directly build FEM basis functions with learnable neural networks.
Unroll finite-difference time-stepping into an iterative neural architecture that produces operator coefficients.
Use numerical analysis to derive convergence and error bounds for the resulting discretized neural operators.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments with reduced errors and improved parameter efficiency, along with convergence error estimates showing polynomial network-size dependence on the target L2 accuracy.
watch_item: The approach may be tightly coupled to the chosen discretization and PDE class, so generalization beyond the numerical scheme used in training should be checked carefully.
paper_title: Numerical Neural Operator: Connection Between Numerical Analysis and the Operator Learning and Building Discretized Neural Operators from Finite Element Methods
